newsitem.title: POLAND: BPH eyes 5 pct stake in Warta.
newsitem.headline: BPH eyes 5 pct stake in Warta.

text.p: Poland's Bank Przemyslowo- Handlowy SA (BPH) wants to acquire about five percent of insurer TUiR Warta by subscribing to its new issue, the BPH president said on Monday.
Warta plans to issue between 865,380 and 2,596,139 shares in February to BPH, Kredyt Bank, Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) and two current shareholders.
"I think (our stake) in Warta will not be higher than five percent of the raised share capital... if more it will not be much more," Henryka Pieronkiewicz told reporters.
She said, however, the bank had yet to decide whether it would join a banking-insurance group, expected to embrace BPH, Warta, PBK, Kredyt Bank and Polish Development Bank (PBR).
She said BPH's participation in the group would depend on final analyses the bank was carrying out.
"There is no decision...by the end of February we will have to take the decision...we have ordered additional analysis to be done...and then we will decide," she said.
She said that even if BPH did not join the group, it was still interested in the Warta stake, as it wanted to gain presence on the insurance market.
Currently Warta has 3.46 million shares outstanding and its main stockholders are the state treasury, with a 34.7 percent stake and Elektrim with 10.1 percent.
